what_its_for: Brodalumab is used to treat moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis (a skin condition that causes red, scaly patches) in adults who have not gotten enough relief from other treatments. It works by blocking a protein in your body that causes inflammation and skin cell buildup.
how_to_take: Brodalumab is given as a shot (injection) under your skin (subcutaneous injection). It comes in a prefilled autoinjector pen. You can inject it into your stomach area (abdomen), thighs, or upper arms. Do not inject into skin that is red, bruised, tender, hard, or affected by psoriasis. Rotate your injection sites each time. Your healthcare provider will show you how to inject it properly before you use it at home.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 210 mg (one injection) given at Weeks 0, 1, and 2. After that, you will take 210 mg once every 2 weeks. Always follow the exact schedule your doctor gives you. Use it on the same day every 2 weeks to help you remember.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, inject it as soon as you remember. Then restart your regular 2-week schedule from that date. Do not give yourself two doses at the same time or on the same day to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store brodalumab in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep it in the original carton to protect it from light. Do not freeze it — if it has been frozen, throw it away. If needed, you can keep it at room temperature (up to 77°F / 25°C) for up to 14 days, but once it reaches room temperature do not put it back in the refrigerator. Throw it away if not used within those 14 days. Keep it out of reach of children. Dispose of used pens in a sharps container — never in regular trash.
what_to_avoid: Do not receive any live vaccines (such as MMR, chickenpox, or nasal flu vaccine) while using brodalumab without talking to your doctor first. Avoid being around people who are sick with infections. Do not start this medication if you have Crohn's disease, as it may make it worse. Avoid drinking alcohol excessively, as it can affect your immune system.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you have: thoughts of suicide or self-harm (this is a serious risk — a special safety program called REMS is required for this medication), signs of serious infection such as fever, chills, cough, or painful urination, new or worsening stomach pain or bowel problems (possible Crohn's disease flare), signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, difficulty breathing, or swelling of your face or throat, or any unusual changes in your mood or behavior.
when_it_works: Some patients see improvement in their skin within 2 to 4 weeks, but it may take up to 12 to 16 weeks to see the full benefit. Keep using the medication as prescribed even if you do not notice changes right away. If you have not seen improvement after several weeks, talk to your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: It is not known if brodalumab is safe during pregnancy or if it passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Children: Brodalumab is not approved for use in patients under 18 years old. Elderly: Older adults can use this medication, but talk to your doctor about any additional concerns. Weakened immune system: Use with caution if you have a history of recurring infections or a condition that weakens your immune system.
